title: Prune
lede: How /prune runs every quality lens on a branch, then fixes the findings through the full feature chain instead of a one-shot patch.

audit.name: Audit
audit.role: Run the correctness and structure reviews, read-only, and collect one findings table.
details: Structure: the /simplify checklist, applied without auto-fix.
qs: When is /prune worth it instead of running /simplify alone?

design.name: Design doc
design.role: Write the findings and how each kind will be fixed into design.md.
details: Findings get IDs (F-01 and on) and are grouped by class, not handled one by one.
Written to `docs/quality-<branch-short>/design.md` (the last segment of the branch name), committed, then /design-review auto-fixes it.

prd.name: PRD
prd.role: Turn the findings into user stories without re-interviewing.
details: It names which fixes are risky enough to need tests.

tdd.name: TDD
tdd.role: Build the fixes in slices, one group of fixes per slice, then refine.
details: The review at the end of this step is the only pause.

pr.name: Pull request
pr.role: Open a PR whose body lists the findings and which IDs were addressed.
risks: At any step, stop, pause or just answer from the owner halts the run at once.

lens.d: One review angle: correctness or structure.

prd.d: Product requirements document: the problem, the solution and the user stories.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand how scaffold's /prune skill turns a quality audit into a planned, tested cleanup PR.
